newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK CORE INFLATION EASED TO 7.5PCT Y/Y IN JAN.
newsitem.headline: GREEK CORE INFLATION EASED TO 7.5PCT Y/Y IN JAN.

text.p: Greece's core inflation eased to 7.5 percent year-on-year in January from 7.7 percent in December based on the revised CPI index introduced for the first time in January, an economist at a foreign bank told Reuters.
Core inflation does not include volatile food and energy prices.
Revised core inflation stood at 6.7 percent year-on-year in October, 7.5 percent in November, he said.
This means that core inflation declined by less than headline inflation which dropped sharply to 6.8 percent year-on-year in January from 7.3 percent in December.

It also shows that a good portion, 0.3 percent, of the month-on-month decline in headline inflation is explained by lower fresh fruit and vegetable prices and smaller rises in motor fuel and heating oil prices.
Fresh fruit and vegetable prices are affected by weather conditions which affect supply. Good weather has been responsible for larger supplies of those goods this year.
Drachma denominated energy prices are determined by world oil prices and the $/drachma rate.
Milder northern hemisphere temperatures have depressed heating oil demand prices while increased supplies of Iraqi crude have crushed the oil winter rally driving crude prices lower.

The National Statistics Service does not release core inflation figures but it is known that the central bank and the national economy ministry trace it. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
